design_prompt:
ZONE1 KITCHEN — CANONICAL PUBLICATION BRIEF

PURPOSE
Help a reader compare capacity, counter space and care. Products and buying decisions first; evidence available without making the page look like an audit dashboard. The configured publication is https://kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone1/.

LAYOUT AND BRAND
Use the warm-paper / forest-green design tokens in publication/theme.css, self-hosted DM Serif Display headings and DM Sans body/UI. Use a masthead, four simple reader links, then the exact Associate disclosure in a visible strip immediately BELOW the masthead on every page. Repeat it in the footer. One native Workspace menu holds all owner/evidence pages; the footer repeats direct access and a complete index. No sidebar, audit-stat hero, revenue scenario or sticky purchase overlay on reader pages.

Lead with a short buying question, three concise format/product cards, a contextual comparison route, practical guides and one modest seasonal feature. Product pages explain who might compare the format, what is documented, and what must be checked. The comparison uses source-linked model-specific capacity, footprint, power and care, not a winner score.

EVIDENCE AND LINKS
Keep the five exact submitted URLs. Observed redirect/title/ASIN, intended listing/ASIN, confirmation date/source and enrolled-account tests are separate fields. shopnow047c-20 is selected but unvalidated and unapplied; never invent approval or add it before the required tests. Every actual outbound product destination is sponsored. Main CTAs say Amazon and repeat the intended-listing/attribution caveat. Every numeric table row has primary evidence; unknown factual values stay blank and visibly flagged.

There is no authorised Amazon price/rating integration. Say that, rather than claiming Amazon bans every permitted price display. Brand snapshots are dated and labelled. No current offer, discount, rating, test, serving yield, performance ranking or personal experience is inferred. Flag F96 records conflicting cord instructions inside the Emeril manual: do not select the permissive version.

AUTHORSHIP, IMAGERY AND VOICE
Byline the publication and disclose AI-assisted document research. Do not invent a human editor or an expert persona. Use original format diagrams labelled not to scale. The one conceptual AI kitchen scene is decorative, visibly labelled and not a photograph/test of a specific model. Actual product photography needs original work or documented rights.

Write in plain, question-led language. Be specific without stuffing paragraphs with table display labels. State the useful trade-off, its source and the consequence. Avoid sweeping superlatives, fabricated social proof, fake urgency, generic intros and filler. “Trendy” means an editorial hypothesis unless dated first-party evidence establishes demand.

CONTENT AND READER LOOP
Use the four existing intent clusters. Improve the canonical answer to a question before adding a competing article. The operating plan is weekly source review and at most one useful new/substantially revised guide per fortnight, published only after claims/source/link/disclosure/build checks. It is not an unattended scheduler. RSS is the working reader-subscription mechanism; no fake email form.

SEARCH AND MEASUREMENT
Keep one canonical reader sitemap, regenerated feed, appropriate index/noindex metadata and truthful JSON-LD. Source-read dates are not publication timestamps. The optional Search Console token stays blank without real property verification. No traffic/ranking promise.

The five measurement events are defined, with only four emitted by a browser. The first-party aggregate collector is implemented/tested, not deployed; the ledger is empty. Keep collection disabled until controlled same-origin hosting, infrastructure-log minimisation and privacy approval exist. Orders come only from authorised reports. No projection, conversion score or placement-improvement claim without dated eligible first-party data.

ACCEPTANCE
Run build.py, verify.py, root/platform tests, annex reproducibility and link/source gates. Audit real rendered pages on narrow/desktop viewports and without JavaScript; check disclosure order/visibility, navigation, keyboard focus, overflow, local assets and outbound link qualification. Keep historical generators read-only. Open this branch’s PR, wait for checks, merge by explicit PR number and confirm the actual deployed Pages content before logging completion.

voice_rules.rule: One topic per page, and every page stamps when its sources were read
voice_rules.why: Focus for the reader, freshness signal for search engines, and an honest record of what the page is based on.

voice_rules.rule: Human voice: contractions, questions, specific numbers instead of 'very/really/incredible', short and long sentences mixed
voice_rules.why: The single fastest way to stop reading like generated filler. Specifics are also the only thing this site has - every number is sourced.

voice_rules.rule: Label vendor claims: anything the manufacturer says about its own product is marked a brand claim, not a tested fact
voice_rules.why: A repeated brand claim presented as an finding is the classic fake-review pattern; labelling it is both honest and compliant.

voice_rules.rule: Working titles are questions or decisions a reader types - never announcements like 'The Ultimate Guide to...'
voice_rules.why: Announcement titles are the loudest AI-slop tell, and they match no search query anyone types.

voice_rules.rule: Headlines name the thing and the payoff; no curiosity-gap clickbait
voice_rules.why: A reader arriving from search must know in one second what the page does for them. Curiosity gaps earn clicks and lose trust, and trust is this site's only product.

voice_rules.rule: Numbers in headlines only when the page sources them in the body
voice_rules.why: A headline number is a promise the body has to keep; an unsourced one is the slop tell readers notice first.

voice_rules.rule: Seasonal pages carry their year and their expiry, and never a countdown
voice_rules.why: Seasonal content must age honestly. Countdown timers are urgency theatre and contradict the site's deliberate no-Amazon-prices rule (Program Policies 2(b)).

voice_rules.rule: A product page may say what a machine is for and what to check before buying. It may not say what it is like to live with.
voice_rules.why: The first is a reading of published documents; the second is an experience nobody here has had, and FTC guidance makes having used the product the test for describing it.

voice_rules.rule: A published brand price is a dated brand snapshot, never an Amazon/current-offer claim. Amazon content display requires the applicable authorised route, not a blanket policy slogan.
voice_rules.why: Silence about price reads as an omission; an unlabelled price reads as today's price. Naming both the figure and the policy that keeps the other one off the page is the version a reader can check.

snapshot.design_prompt:
ZONE1 KITCHEN — DESIGN PROMPT (paste-ready)
Goal: polish this Amazon affiliate site so it reads like a human-run marketing publication — not an AI-generated data dump — without weakening its verification discipline.

SITE AS IT IS TODAY (do not contradict these facts)
- Static site generated by build.py from data/*.json; live at https://kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone1/
- Three tracked air fryers (Chefman 6 Qt dual-basket, Emeril 26 QT French-door oven, Chefman 8 Qt single-basket). The supplied Amazon short links resolve to candidate ASINs whose product identity is UNCONFIRMED and must stay labelled as such.
- Every published number carries a source badge (S1-S31) linking to the official page it came from. Values that cannot be confirmed are left blank and listed on the Flagged-for-review page — never guessed, never back-filled.
- Amazon prices, star ratings and review counts are NEVER displayed (Amazon Program Policies 2(b) and 6(t)). Manufacturer list prices are allowed when cited to the brand's own page.
- No hands-on testing is ever claimed; no superlative ("best", "top-rated") is asserted as fact; vendor statements are labelled as brand claims.
- An affiliate disclosure bar sits above the header on every page: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."

DESIGN DIRECTION
1. Keep the dashboard skeleton — sticky sidebar, top bar, disclosure band, stat tiles, sourced tables — and keep the landing page editorial: one-sentence value proposition above the fold, then a format finder, then sourced article cards.
2. Palette (shipped pass 12, 2026-11-16 — reuse these tokens, do not invent new colors): warm paper #f5f1e8, cream cards #fffdf7, aged-paper #efe9d8, ink #212821, brand deep green #245746 (deep #16382e), terracotta accent #b05a2f, hairlines #e4ddc9; ok/warn/bad/info tints are CSS variables. All 23 foreground/background pairs were measured at >= 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) during the pass-12 audit.
3. Typography: serif display via --serif (Iowan Old Style / Palatino / Georgia stack) for headings and hero, system sans for UI and body; sentence case; tight letter-spacing on display sizes. Source badges (.src) render as quiet footnote-style chips, never as buttons, so prose stays readable.
4. Components that must survive any redesign: source badge (S#), blank cell with "not confirmed" pill, flag pill, stat tile, callout variants (info/warn/bad), comparison table with per-cell source links, disclosure bar.
5. Shipped structure (pass 12, 2026-11-16 — keep on any future redesign): topbar with compact primary nav (Picks / Buying guide / Articles / Compare) plus verified-data stamp; sidebar grouped Shop smart / Products / Trust & evidence / Owner workspace; deep-green footer; decorative artwork is stroke-only inline SVG (three format glyphs) — no photography, per D-5.
6. Mobile-first: single column below 820px, tap targets at least 40px, no horizontal scroll, prefers-reduced-motion respected, focus-visible outlines kept.
7. Page inventory to keep: Home, This week's picks, Buying guide, Articles, Category, three product pages, Comparison, Full dataset, Compliance, Flagged, Suggestions, Questions, Decisions & handover, Executive summary, Re-verification, Platform, Previous passes, Design prompt pack.

EDITORIAL VOICE (anti-AI-slop rules - non-negotiable)
- No unverified superlatives: never "best", "top-rated", "revolutionary", "must-have", "game-changing". If it is not sourced, do not say it.
- Specific numbers beat intensifiers. Contractions and questions are welcome. Mix short and long sentences.
- Show the gaps: blank cells, published conflicts and "unconfirmed" badges are content, not bugs.
- Label every manufacturer statement as a brand claim, not a tested fact.
- Never write "we tested", "our pick", "in our kitchen". The site does not test products.
- One topic per page; every page stamps when its sources were read.
- Banned openers and claim guards are enforced in build.py (see decisions.html, anti-slop list).

SEO LAYER (already implemented - keep it)

ADDENDUM - 2026-11-16 (session arena/19d92a81) - MARKETING AND ORGANIC-TRAFFIC LAYER
The brief for this pass: make the site read like a polished marketing affiliate publication
with catchy, trendy, product-related articles that can earn organic traffic - and never like
AI slop. Directives below extend, and never replace, the rules above.

1. READ LIKE A PUBLICATION, NOT AN ADMIN PANEL. Pass 12 grouped the sidebar into
   Shop smart / Products / Trust & evidence / Owner workspace and set the visual system;
   what remains is a production-method byline on every money page (SG-32) and one brand
   name on every surface (SG-33, question Q-25). The evidence layer stays one click away:
   honesty is a feature of the voice, not the layout.
2. CATCHY, TRENDY, SOURCE-LED CONTENT. Ship seasonal and query-led pieces four to six
   weeks before the retail moment (T-9; the parallel pass's SG-24 says the same from the
   other side: ship while the season is live). Three proven templates in this niche: the
   deal-safety investigation (the model-number switch, published), the gift/buying guide
   matched to people and kitchens (published), and the according-to-the-manuals care guide
   (published). Trendy never means unverified: the sourcing rules above are unchanged.
3. ORGANIC TRAFFIC PROGRAM. Four clusters with hub pages and generator-maintained
   internal links (SG-35); one target query per article; Search Console verification and
   sitemap submission the moment the owner can (account-only, T-3); and the reader-capture
   decision their SG-30 opens (the RSS feed itself shipped in pass 12).
4. IMAGERY. Typographic on purpose until image rights exist - the parallel pass's SG-23
   and Q-22 settle the licensing question; NEVER AI-generated product imagery; if images
   arrive, they are Amazon-licensed or original, with factual alt text.
5. WHAT 'NOT AI SLOP' MEANS HERE. Specific over sweeping. Sourced over smooth. Opinion
   labelled as judgement. Gaps shown as gaps. Freshness dated. A voice that would rather
   be interesting than comprehensive. The banned-phrase guard in build.py is the floor,
   not the ceiling. (V-5..V-7.)

voice_rules.rule: One topic per page, and every page stamps when its sources were read
voice_rules.why: Focus for the reader, freshness signal for search engines, and an honest record of what the page is based on.

voice_rules.rule: Human voice: contractions, questions, specific numbers instead of 'very/really/incredible', short and long sentences mixed
voice_rules.why: The single fastest way to stop reading like generated filler. Specifics are also the only thing this site has - every number is sourced.

voice_rules.rule: Label vendor claims: anything the manufacturer says about its own product is marked a brand claim, not a tested fact
voice_rules.why: A repeated brand claim presented as an finding is the classic fake-review pattern; labelling it is both honest and compliant.

voice_rules.rule: Working titles are questions or decisions a reader types - never announcements like 'The Ultimate Guide to...'
voice_rules.why: Announcement titles are the loudest AI-slop tell, and they match no search query anyone types.

voice_rules.rule: Headlines name the thing and the payoff; no curiosity-gap clickbait
voice_rules.why: A reader arriving from search must know in one second what the page does for them. Curiosity gaps earn clicks and lose trust, and trust is this site's only product.

voice_rules.rule: Numbers in headlines only when the page sources them in the body
voice_rules.why: A headline number is a promise the body has to keep; an unsourced one is the slop tell readers notice first.

voice_rules.rule: Seasonal pages carry their year and their expiry, and never a countdown
voice_rules.why: Seasonal content must age honestly. Countdown timers are urgency theatre and contradict the site's deliberate no-Amazon-prices rule (Program Policies 2(b)).

voice_rules.rule: A product page may say what a machine is for and what to check before buying. It may not say what it is like to live with.
voice_rules.why: The first is a reading of published documents; the second is an experience nobody here has had, and FTC guidance makes having used the product the test for describing it.

voice_rules.rule: A price on this site is a brand's own list price, labelled as such, with the reason Amazon's figure is absent in the same breath.
voice_rules.why: Silence about price reads as an omission; an unlabelled price reads as today's price. Naming both the figure and the policy that keeps the other one off the page is the version a reader can check.
